[officer of the watch] Aye, Captain. We ghost toward the Road and anchor at about 2 miles from the port, wherever that falls. I understand your hands' rule, and I will take it as the limit. I will not order the boats out. The Great Road lies WNW, 3½ miles by account. The pilot said the road is half a mile off Castle Cornet. By your rule we would need to be within 2 miles of the port. That is about 1½ miles of westing from here, and then we would anchor. At the present creep, about a cable in five minutes, that is a long time away, so the real air is what matters. I will keep the yards trimmed by hand if the wind changes, take fixes every 5 minutes, and let you know when we come within 2½ miles of Castle Cornet. The soundings will tell us the bottom: the pilot said 9 to 16 fathoms of fine sand in the road. I have not found less than 19 fathoms yet. I will ask for the best bower when the lead shows 15 to 16 fathoms or less. That is your word to give.
[officer of the watch] The officer of the watch stands by until 5 minutes have passed; the standing orders hold the deck.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 13:45. You shaped for the Great Road of Guernsey at 13:41: WNW by account, 3 miles, and the helm gives W by N (284°). The log says: "the line passes the shore under St Peter Port within two cables. Allowing the flood, two knots to the NE, no course makes it good at her present way of one knot; W by N loses least." That is the master's own word that at a knot we cannot beat the flood, but the fixes show a different tide, and we have not been set north. I trust the fixes. At 13:45 the wind is E at 3 knots, 165° right astern, and I trimmed the yards to it at your order. We have about a knot of way, W by N (283°). Fix at 13:45 by Herm N, Sark E and St Martin's Point W, within 3 cables: 49°26'N, 2°27'W, good to 2 cables. The account moved a cable S by W. Castle Cornet is 3 miles by account. **The line passes the shore under St Peter Port within two cables.** That is the log's warning. We should not stand so close in, even at a knot, with the flood setting us across and 16 fathoms to 24½ by the chart. We have 2 miles to run before we reach your rule of 2 miles from the port. The pilot's marks help: the guard-house open SE of Castle Cornet clears the Têtes d'Aval, and the town church open N of the castle brings us to the road. The land about Jethou is on the starboard bow, NW, 2 miles. Jethou NNW, 3 miles. The Little Russel NW by N, 2 miles. Roustel NNW, 3½ miles. The Hanois are W, 3½ leagues. I will report at 2½ miles from the Castle.
[officer of the watch] The officer of the watch stands by until 5 minutes have passed; the standing orders hold the deck.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 13:50. We are ghosting W by N with the wind E at 3 knots, right astern at 170°. I trimmed the yards to it, and the sheets stand as trimmed. The fix at 13:50 by Herm N by E, St Martin's Point W and Sark E, within 4 cables, puts us at 49°26'N, 2°27'W, good to 3 cables. The account moved two cables SW, so we make about 2 cables in five minutes. That is half a knot over the ground. Castle Cornet is about 3 miles WNW. At that rate it will take 4 or 5 hours to reach your 2-mile line, and the tide turns at about 15:45, which should help. The flood now sets 1¾ knots NE by the tables and the fixes do not show it. The land about Jethou is NW by N, 2 miles. St Martin's Point is W, 4 miles. The depth is 22 fathoms by the chart. I have nothing more to try with the sails. Studdingsails are set, all head sheets are aft, and the yards are square to the wind. If a breeze comes, I will brace to it. Fix every 5 minutes.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:00. The log was hove at 1¾ knots, and the breeze is in. The wind is 5 knots from the ESE, apparent 147° on the starboard quarter, and we make 2 knots, steering NW by W (303°) by your 13:58 order. I have braced the yards to the wind. The sheets stand as trimmed. The hands are ready on deck. Fix at 14:00 by the Little Russel NW by N, Herm N by E and St Peter Port NW by W, within 7 cables: 49°26'N, 2°28'W, good to 4 cables. The account moved a cable SW. St Peter Port is NW by W, 3 miles. **The land is close.** The land about Jethou is on the starboard bow, NNW, a mile. We are heading NW by W, toward the Little Russel mouth, and Jethou is to starboard of the bow. Roustel is NNW, 3½ miles by account. The pilot warned that Roustel lies in mid-channel and shows only at half ebb. With the flood still running and the tide turning about 15:45, it will not show. Herm is N by E, 2 miles. St Martin's Point W, 4 miles. The depth is 24 fathoms by the chart, and no bottom at 20. **The Great Road lies off the town, half a mile from Castle Cornet.** The pilot's marks, the guard-house open SE of Castle Cornet and the town church open N of the castle, are our guides. The lookout has not yet called them. We are 3 miles off at 2 knots, so about 1½ hours to the 2-mile line, and a little more to the road itself. Your rule says anchor at about 2 miles. I will ask for the best bower when the depth comes to 16 fathoms or less, or at your word. Fixes every 5 minutes, soundings every 10.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:05. The yards are braced at 130° on the starboard quarter and the sheets stand as trimmed. The hands have all turned out, 113 on deck. We steer NW by W (304°) at about 2 knots, with the wind ESE at 5 knots. **We are not closing the town.** Castle Cornet is still 3 miles by account, as it was at 13:45 and at 13:58. The fix at 14:05 by the Little Russel NNW, Herm NNE and Jethou N by E met in a point: 49°26'N, 2°28'W, good to 2 cables, and the account moved only a cable WSW. Our course made good is SW by W (236°) while we steer NW by W. That means a set of about 70° to starboard of our heading, and it takes our headway. The log's flood, 1¾ knots NE, is not what the fixes show. We are being set across our track, SW, toward St Martin's Point and the shore W of Jethou, not toward the Road. If this goes on, we will be carried south of the Great Road, onto the east side of the Little Russel's approaches and nearer St Martin's Point. I would like you to see this, as the helm is yours. A heading further north, NNW (about 330°), would offset the set. That brings Jethou and the Little Russel mouth closer. The pilot's marks are the right guide, and I have not got them in sight yet. The depth is 25 fathoms by the chart, and no bottom at 20. Roustel NNW, 3½ miles. I am fixing every 5 minutes.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:11. You came up a point at 14:06 to NW (315°), and the wind has settled at E, 4 knots, 108° on the starboard quarter. I have braced the yards and trimmed the spanker sheet. The topmast studdingsails, courses, topsails and topgallants were shaking as the wind drew round. They should draw now. Fix at 14:11 by the Little Russel NNW, St Martin's Point W and Sark E, within 7 cables: 49°26'N, 2°28'W, good to 4 cables. Over the ground we still make good SW by W (238°) at about 1½ knots, with the flood now only ¾ knot by the tables. I do not trust that. **Marks.** - St Peter Port NW by W, 3 miles (the account says 2½ miles by the Great Road). - St Martin's Point W, 3 miles. The Little Russel NNW, 2 miles. - The land about Jethou is N by W, a mile, on the starboard bow. Jethou N by E, 3 miles. Herm NNE, 2 miles. - Roustel N by W, 3½ miles. The Hanois W, 3 leagues. - The depth is 18½ fathoms by the chart, and no bottom at 20. The depth has come down from 25 fathoms to 18½, so we are climbing the bank toward the Road. The pilot said 9 to 16 fathoms there. The land about Jethou is on the starboard bow, a mile. Our heading NW is heading well to the west of it, so it will pass on the starboard hand. I will keep fixing and sounding.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:16. Castle Cornet is now 2 miles by account, so we are at your anchoring line. The Great Road bears NW, 2½ miles by account. Fix at 14:16 by the Little Russel NNW, St Martin's Point W and Brecqhou E, within 4 cables: 49°26'N, 2°29'W, good to 2 cables. We steer NW (315°), 2 knots, with the wind E at 3 knots, 108° on the starboard quarter, and all sail set, studdingsails and all. **The depth is 24½ fathoms by the chart**, with no bottom at 20 on the last cast, seven minutes ago. The pilot said the Road is 9 to 16 fathoms on very fine sand, half a mile from the castle. So we are not in the Road. We are at your 2-mile line, in 24 fathoms, with the Great Russel's bank behind us. If you wish to anchor here, as you said for your hands' rule, the bottom was fine sand at 25 fathoms at 13:07. Another half-mile NW should bring us into 16 fathoms and the pilot's holding ground, but your boats' rule sets 2 miles. **The land.** The land about Jethou is on the starboard bow, N by W, a mile. St Martin's Point is W, 3 miles. The Little Russel NNW, 2 miles. Herm NNE, 2 miles. Roustel is N by W, 3 miles. **Orders.** I can take in the studdingsails and make ready the best bower, with 240 fathoms of cable. I may not let go on my own word without danger. I would take in the studdingsails and courses first, so she comes to the anchor under topsails. Which would you like?
[officer of the watch] The officer of the watch stands by until a word on deck; the standing orders hold the deck.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:21. All four topmast studdingsails are in and made up (14:19), and the main course is clewed up and hanging in the gear. The fore lower studdingsail booms were already rigged in. I have ordered the other booms rigged in, starboard and larboard of the main topmast, and starboard and larboard of the fore topmast. Four orders are done and in hand. The topgallant booms I did not touch, as the log shows those sails furled with no mention of booms to be run out. I will confirm when the hands report them in. The ship now has topsails, topgallants, fore course and all fore-and-aft sails set, as you ordered. Wind E by S, 0 to 2 knots, almost calm. Apparent wind 147° on the starboard quarter, 0 knots. Fix at 14:21 by the Little Russel NNW, St Martin's Point W and Brecqhou E, within 3 cables: 49°26'N, 2°29'W, good to 2 cables, the account kept. The depth is 25 fathoms by the chart, no bottom at 20. The land about Jethou is close aboard on the starboard bow, N, a mile. St Peter Port NW by W, 3 miles. The Great Road is 2½ miles away. line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:26. The airs are light, E at 2 knots, apparent 157° on the starboard quarter, 1 knot. We hold NW at about a knot, and the fix at 14:26 by the Little Russel NNW, St Martin's Point W and Brecqhou E, within 3 cables, shows 49°26'N, 2°29'W, good to 2 cables, a cable S by E. Castle Cornet is still 2 miles by account, and the Great Road NW, 2 miles. The glass is 30.33, steady, risen a hundredth. The depth is 23 fathoms by the chart, no bottom at 20. The chart warns of 2 fathoms within the account's doubt, somewhere in the doubtful circle near us. I have not seen a shoal, but I note it. The land about Jethou is a mile N by E on the starboard bow. The studdingsail booms are in. The yards and sheets stand as trimmed to the old wind, and the sails give no way to speak of. The tide turns about 15:45, and then the stream may help us. At your 2-mile line, we are there. If you want to anchor now, in 23 fathoms of fine sand, the best bower has 240 fathoms, so the scope is ample. Say so and I will give the order to make ready. Otherwise we keep creeping toward the Road.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Aye, Captain, as you will. We make toward the Road and clear the Great Bank to the west. By the chart orders the Great Bank bears WNW (296°), a mile by account from us. We steer NW (315°). That is 19° to the right of the bank, so our line passes north of it, with the bank to starboard-to-port as it comes abaft the beam. The Road lies NE of the bank, as you say. With the airs light and the account good to 1 to 2 cables, I would hold NW, or come up a point to NNW if you want more clearance, and watch the lead. A cast shallower than 12 fathoms would be warning. The chart gives 2 fathoms within the account's doubt, which I take to be the Great Bank, so keep it well clear to port. The pilot's mark for the road is the town church open north of the castle. I do not yet see it called. Fix at 14:27: 49°26'N, 2°29'W, good to a cable. The Little Russel N by W, St Martin's Point W, Brecqhou E. The land about Jethou is a mile N by E. I will fix every 5 minutes and sound every 10, and I will report each change in the depth.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:37. We still hold NW (321°), by your 14:27 order, creeping in the light ESE airs. Wind 3 knots at most, apparent 159° on the starboard quarter. The yards are braced up a point by your hand, and the log says the yards stand 34° from square. Fix at 14:37 by the Little Russel N by W, St Martin's Point W and the Great Russel ENE, within 2 cables: 49°26'N, 2°29'W, good to 2 cables. The account moved a cable SSW. By the chart, the Great Bank is NW by W (302°), a mile. We are making hardly any headway at all. Our heading is NW (321°) and the Bank is 19° to port of it, so the Bank is just to our left of the bow and about a mile ahead. We pass north of it on this line, but the margin is small, and with the set we may not clear it as you wish. **Depth.** 21 fathoms by the chart, and no bottom at 20. The chart gives 15 to 26 fathoms within the doubt, so the Bank is not yet felt. The pilot's guidance was the guard-house open SE of Castle Cornet, to clear the Têtes d'Aval. I do not see it called. I would come up a point to NNW (about 303° to 337°), which opens the Bank on the larboard bow and clears it more surely. I have not touched the helm. Shall I keep the heading, or alter?

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 14:42. You came up three-quarters of a point at 14:38 to NW by N (329°), and we hold it, with the wind ESE at 3 knots, 143° on the starboard quarter, and the yards braced. The spanker sheet is trimmed. The Great Bank bears NW by W (303°) by the chart, a mile by account, so it is now 26° to port of our heading, a little farther abaft the bow than before. Fix at 14:42 by the Little Russel N by W, St Martin's Point W and the Great Russel ENE, within a cable: 49°26'N, 2°30'W, good to 2 cables. The account moved a cable SW by S. **Depth.** 17 fathoms at low water by the chart, down from 21 at 14:37, with no bottom at 20 on the last cast four minutes ago. We have started up the bank: the chart gives 14½ to 25 fathoms within the account's doubt. That is the first sign of shoaling, so I would take the lead often. The sound order is every 10 minutes. I have not given it. I will not let go on my own word except for an immediate danger. **For the evolution.** - The catalogue says to round to into the wind or the stream, whichever is the stronger. Here the wind is E at 5 knots, light, and the flood sets NNE at about a knot, so we bring up head to the wind, or to the stream if it is the stronger. - The scope is five times the depth. The chart gives 19½ fathoms here, so 100 fathoms of cable on the best bower, which has 240 fathoms. - The last cast gave 18¼ fathoms, very fine sand. **Position.** Fix at 14:50: 49°26'N, 2°30'W. We make good WSW (246°), though we steer N, so the leeway and the set take us west, and our ground track is nowhere near our heading. We are not making ground toward the Road. The fixes bear it out. **The Great Bank** bears NW (318°) by the chart, still a mile by account. It has been a mile for a quarter of an hour. It stays on the larboard bow as we go west, so we are sliding along its south side. The depth is 17 fathoms by the chart, no bottom at 20 on the 14:55 cast. The chart gives 12 to 22 fathoms within the doubt. The land about St Martin's Point is a mile abeam to larboard, WSW, with St Martin's Point 2 miles W. I think you are standing north to clear the Bank and enter the road. The danger is that our ground track, SW of W, puts us on the Bank itself or on the point. I would give her more north, or anchor now. The ground is very fine sand at 17 to 18 fathoms, and the road itself lies half a mile from the Castle, not here. Whichever you choose, I am watching the lead.

We are south-east of it, on the same side as before, getting no nearer the Road. Castle Cornet is 2 miles NW by N, as it was at 14:16. Our ground track is WSW (247°), while we steer N. That is the same set to the west as before, 3° leeway, and the tide. It sets us on the land about St Martin's Point, SW by W a mile on the larboard quarter. If this holds another ten minutes, we shall be in the point's off-lying shoal water. **My advice.** Anchor now. The ground is very fine sand at 15½ to 18 fathoms, the cable is ample, the breeze is fair from the east, which is off the land (the shore at the point is to the SW), and we are 2 miles from the town by your rule. You can pick the Road up on the flood or the morning. If you would rather go on, we must steer NNE or NE by N to make good N. With the helm yours, I will not touch it. The standing orders hold. line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 15:07. The best bower is let go in 20½ fathoms and the cable is veering to 102 fathoms, five times the depth. At 15:07 the log shows 23 fathoms out and the cable slack, strain 0.00. She is riding by the best bower to the ebb, wind and tide together. The log gave a warning that 20½ fathoms is deep to anchor in. The roads lie in 17 fathoms and less, and here she rides on a steep cable and will be long heaving it in. That is a point for the morning. It does not make us unsafe. Fix at 15:07 by the Little Russel N, Castle Cornet NW by N and St Peter Port NW, in a point: 49°26'N, 2°31'W, good to a cable. Castle Cornet is a mile by account. The depth by the chart is 13½ fathoms at the position, with 4 to 19½ fathoms within the doubt. **One warning.** The wind is NE by E at 10 to 11 knots, and the land about St Martin's Point lies SW by W, a mile, close aboard on the larboard quarter. That is dead to leeward. If she drags, the wind sets her straight on that shore, which is only a mile off. The ebb sets SW as well, so wind and tide are together. I suggest: 1. Let her bring up and veer more cable to 120 fathoms or so, if the strain shows. 2. Fix every 5 minutes. The marks Castle Cornet and St Peter Port should hold their bearings. If either swings, she drags. 3. Keep the second anchor ready to let go. That is your word, unless danger is immediate. 4. A hand in the chains with the lead, and the anchor watch set. The sails are in the gear. I will hold the deck, watch the fixes and the cable, and report any change.

She lies NNE, 2.8 knots through the water, with the wind ENE at 12 knots, a moderate breeze. The state shows no sail set. The glass is steady at 30.31, the sky is clear and the sea smooth. **Holding.** The fixes at 15:14, 15:17 and 15:19, by St Martin's Point W, Castle Cornet NW by N and St Peter Port NW by N, all met in a point or within a cable, and the account kept each time. The bearings have not slid in a quarter of an hour, so she is not dragging. **The land.** - The land about St Martin's Point is 8 cables off on the larboard quarter, SW by W. It is dead to leeward, and has stayed 8 cables since 15:14. - St Peter Port is NW by N, 2 miles. Jethou NE, 3 miles. Herm NE, 3 miles. The Little Russel N, 2 miles. The Great Russel ENE, 5 miles. - The depth is 16 fathoms by the chart. **The boat.** The launch is away for the purser, but it is still 'hoisting out'. I will tell you when the launch is clear. The ship is under anchor with all sail in, and the hands are still turned up, 113 on deck. When you wish, I would pipe the watch below and set an anchor watch of the starboard watch, with the lead and a fix every 5 minutes, and the second anchor ready. I will do that on your word, or if you say 'work the ship' for it, as you have said. The standing orders hold: 'Fixes' every 5 minutes (yours), 'sound often' every 5 minutes (mine), and 'tend the sheets' every half hour (nothing to trim at anchor).

note.text: 15:20 AT ANCHOR in the Great Road of Guernsey: best bower, 102 fm out, bar-taut strain 0.02, riding NNE, wind ENE 12 kn. Fixes 15:14/15:17/15:19 (St Martin's Point W, Castle Cornet NW by N, St Peter Port NW by N) steady = not dragging. Land about St Martin's Point 8 cables SW by W dead to leeward; depth 16 fm by chart. All sail in; state 'Sail set: none'. Captain gave me the general authority to work the ship at 15:08 (port business, standing orders, new destination, chase, reckoning by hand and tide, sending for a person kept back). Launch is away with the purser Mr Porter (hoisting out/away) for St Peter Port prices and news. News from pilot: Britain at war with Batavian Republic, France and Spain. Pilot Tostevin £3, purse £844. Captain's remarks: 'Fixes' standing order resumed; my standing orders: 'tend the sheets', 'sound often' (5 min, land <5 mi; 'sound regularly' belayed). Watch below not yet piped; captain's word welcome.

That is the sixth fix in a row with the same bearings, so she is not dragging. Wind NE by E at 11 knots, 36° on the starboard bow, glass 30.32, steady. The depth by the chart is 16½ fathoms, within the 11 to 20 of the doubt. The lead is being hove every 5 minutes. The last cast I read gave no bottom at 20 fathoms, though that was 24 minutes ago, and the chart says 16½, so it is a poor cast. I will ask for a fresh one. The launch is with the purser, away. The ship is riding easy and I see nothing to correct. I will set the anchor watch on your word, and send the watch below if you wish.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, 16:00, eight bells in the first dog watch. We are quiet at anchor and she has not stirred in 50 minutes. **Holding.** The fix at 16:00 by St Martin's Point W and Castle Cornet NW by N, cut at 55°: 49°26'N, 2°31'W, good to a cable, the account kept within a cable. The bearings are the same as at 15:07. The cable is bar-taut at 0.02 of its rating, 102 fathoms out. **Soundings.** Since 15:25 every five minutes the lead has given 18 to 18½ fathoms by the chart on very fine sand, with the 1½ fathoms of tide allowed: 19½, 19¼, 19½, 19¾ and 19¼ by the cast. Today's soundings are steady within a quarter fathom. The last cast, 4 minutes ago, gave 19 fathoms, very fine sand. **Weather.** The wind backed to NE by E at 15:54, a moderate breeze, 11 knots. The sky has become hazy and the visibility is a few miles. The glass is 30.31, down 2 hundredths in three hours. Nothing to alarm, but I will watch it. The land about St Martin's Point, 8 cables SW by W, is dead to leeward, so I would rather have a second anchor ready if the wind freshens. **Using your general authority:** I piped down the watch at the change. The larboard watch has the deck, the starboard watch below. I did so because there are 113 hands on deck with nothing to do. The launch is still away, with the purser, on the long passage, and the log says 'hoisting out'. I will hail you when she is alongside. I have not touched the port's business or the standing orders. The anchor watch is the larboard watch, with the lead every 5 minutes and a fix every 5 minutes.

line.text: [officer of the watch] Captain, I looked into the boat and I think you have found a fault in the game, not a mistake in the handling. **What the log and readings show:** - 15:10: you ordered 'send the boat ashore with the purser'. The log said "Not hands enough on deck to send boat; the hands are coming to anchor". The work stood as 'sending boat (for hands)', waiting on the anchor evolution. - 15:14 and 15:19: the readings still list 'sending boat (for hands)' among the work waiting. - 15:23: brought up. At 15:24 the readings show only 'heaving lead' in hand, and the waiting boat work is gone. It never became 'doing'. - 15:24: your second order was refused, "Mr Porter is in the boat". So the purser is still sitting in the launch. - Since then, every reading says "the launch away for the prices and what news there is, hoisting out", and 'Mr Porter, purser: in the boat'. Today the readings say 'work_in_hand: nothing in hand'. At 16:00 your 'Belay sending the boat ashore' was refused: "There is no work in hand or waiting to belay." So the boat is marked as hoisting out with no evolution behind it. It looks as if the waiting boat work was lost when the 'coming to anchor' work finished, and now the launch and the purser are stuck in that state. **What I tried.** 'Hoist out the launch' was not understood (it takes 'out' for a spar). 'Send the launch ashore' was refused to me, as the boat's errands ashore are the port's business and kept back from my general authority. It may be allowed by name ('you may send the boat'). I did not pipe down the watch before the work vanished. The pipe-down at 16:00 came after the work was already gone, so I do not think I caused it. **Things you might try:** 1. Call the purser from the boat ('call the purser', which sends for a person and is yours), which may clear his 'in the boat' state, then send the boat again. 2. Send the cutter (23 ft, 6 oars) or the jolly boat instead. That leaves the launch stuck. 3. Allow me by name ('you may send the boat'), and I will try. It may meet the same refusal. I have noted it in my journal for the record. The ship is as safe as she was: at anchor, holding by fixes since 15:07.

note.text: 16:05 BUG NOTE (for the captain/developer): the 'send the boat ashore with the purser' order of 15:10 was queued as 'sending boat (for hands)' while all hands were 'coming to anchor'. It showed in work_in_hand as waiting at 15:14 and 15:19, then was gone at 15:24 after 'brought up' (15:23) without ever starting. The boat reading has since stuck at 'the launch away for the prices and what news there is, hoisting out'; people: 'Mr Porter, purser: in the boat'; work_in_hand: nothing in hand. Captain's re-send at 15:24 refused ('Mr Porter is in the boat'); 'Belay sending the boat ashore' refused at 16:00 ('no work in hand or waiting to belay'). My own tries: 'Hoist out the launch' not understood; 'Send the launch ashore' refused as port business (kept back from general authority; may be allowed by name). Suggested: 'call the purser' then re-send; or send the cutter; or allow me by name. Not caused by my pipe-down at 16:00, which came after the work had vanished.

note.text: 16:08 STAND-DOWN JOURNAL for whoever sits here next (and for the replay if the captain rolls the save back). SITUATION at 16:07: Brig Harpy at anchor in the Great Road of Guernsey, best bower, 102 fm out, cable bar-taut strain 0.02, riding NNE, wind NE by E 11 kn (backed 15:54), glass 30.32, hazy. Holding: all fixes since 15:07 identical (St Martin's Point W, Castle Cornet NW by N, St Peter Port NW by N); 49°26'N 2°30'W; depth 18-19 fm by chart/lead, very fine sand. Land about St Martin's Point SW by W 8 cables is dead to leeward; second anchor on captain's word (or my own if she drags). All sail furled; larboard watch has the deck (piped down 16:00). Purse £844, 16 t copper ore, water 45 t, provisions 120 d. Pilot news: Britain at war with Batavian Republic, France, Spain. BUG: 'send the boat ashore with the purser' at 15:10 waited for hands during anchoring and vanished at 15:23; launch stuck 'away, hoisting out', purser 'in the boat', cannot be called, no other boat can be sent. AFTER A REPLAY, DO THIS: give the boat order only once the ship is brought up and hands are free; do not queue it behind 'coming to anchor'. THINGS I LEARNED: (1) the chart tool returns NO image to me, only a placeholder line; never describe a chart picture; use 'the bearing by the chart of X' and 'the distance to X' orders (X must be a mark such as Herm, Castle Cornet, the Great Bank, St Peter Port; 'the distance to <lat long>' works). (2) After brace orders say 'Trim the sails'; in a calm the captain braces by hand ('brace the yards up two points'). (3) Standing orders in force: 'tend the sheets' (half hour), 'sound often' (5 min, land<5 mi), captain's 'Fixes' (5 min, land<3 mi). (4) Captain's general authority covers sail, anchors, helm, lead, fixes; port's business incl. boats ashore only by name ('you may send the boat'). (5) Tides near Guernsey: master's tables said NE flood but fixes showed we were set WSW and made no ground; trust the fixes. (6) Anchoring: scope 5x depth; the log warned 20.5 fm is deep for the road (17 fm and less). (7) Pilot Tostevin's marks: guard-house open SE of Castle Cornet clears Têtes d'Aval; town church open N of castle for the Road; Great Road 9-16 fm fine sand half a mile off Castle Cornet; HW St Peter Port ~22:30 rise 25 ft.
